Delivery Pipeline
data.description: Drill in for the release path

steps.title: Shopper places an order
steps.narration: The storefront sends CreateOrder through CloudFront to the API Gateway with an Idempotency-Key header.

steps.title: Gateway routes to Order Service
steps.narration: Token validated against Okta JWKS, then routed over gRPC.

steps.title: Idempotency check
steps.narration: A replayed key returns the stored response; a new key continues into the handler.

steps.title: Reserve stock and authorize payment
steps.narration: Inventory is held for 15 minutes, then Payment Service authorizes the card via Stripe.

steps.title: Commit order + outbox atomically
steps.narration: One database transaction writes the order and its OrderPlaced outbox row.

steps.title: Event fan-out
steps.narration: The outbox relay publishes to MSK; fulfillment and (soon) recommendations consume it.

steps.title: Authorization fails
steps.narration: Stripe returns a decline, or the call times out after 1.5s.

steps.title: Bounded retries
steps.narration: Transient failures retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff.

steps.title: Release the hold and return 402
steps.narration: Inventory is released immediately rather than waiting for the TTL (#RISK-2).

steps.title: Async confirmation via webhook
steps.narration: 3-D Secure flows complete later; Stripe notifies Payment Service by webhook.

steps.title: Feature branch to PR
steps.narration: Every change lands through a reviewed PR with CODEOWNERS approval.

steps.title: Merge, tag, build, test
steps.narration: Signed images are built once and promoted, never rebuilt per environment.

steps.title: Progressive delivery
steps.narration: A 5% canary behind checkout_v2_enabled; an SLO breach rolls back automatically.

steps.title: Synced to the cluster
steps.narration: Argo CD reconciles the region. Remember the holiday freeze (#CON-3).

items.title: Reduce checkout abandonment by 15%
items.body:
Baseline abandonment is **68%** (GA4, Q2 2026). Target **58%** by end of Q1 2027.

Primary levers: guest checkout (#REQ-1), faster payment authorization (#REQ-3).

items.title: 99.95% availability on the checkout path
items.body:
Measured as successful `CreateOrder` responses / valid attempts over a rolling 28 days.

| Window | Error budget |
|---|---|
| 28 days | 20m 9s |
| Holiday peak week | 5m 2s |

items.title: PCI DSS 4.0 compliance before holiday peak
items.body: Pass the QSA assessment by **Nov 13** so the CDE is certified before Black Friday. See #EPIC-4.

items.title: Guest checkout
items.body:
Shoppers can complete a purchase without creating an account.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Email is the only required identity field
- [ ] Guest orders can be claimed after sign-up
- [ ] Guest tokens are scoped to a single order

items.title: Idempotent order creation
items.body: Retrying `POST /v2/orders` with the same `Idempotency-Key` must never create a second order. Keys are retained for 24h. Root cause context: #BUG-1.

items.title: Payment authorization p95 under 2s
items.body: Measured from Order Service request to Stripe authorization result, excluding 3-D Secure challenges.

items.title: Real-time inventory reservation
items.body: Stock is held at checkout for 15 minutes and released on payment failure or expiry. Mitigates #RISK-2.

items.title: Typo-tolerant product search
items.body: Queries with up to two character edits return relevant results (e.g. `sneekers` -> sneakers).

items.title: Catalog read latency p99 under 150ms
items.body: For `GET /v2/products/{sku}` at 8x baseline traffic (#ASM-1).

items.title: Order events are published effectively-once
items.body: Every committed order produces exactly one `OrderPlaced` event as observed by consumers (at-least-once delivery + consumer de-duplication).

items.title: Distributed tracing across the checkout path
items.body: A single trace spans gateway -> order -> payment -> Stripe and continues through Kafka headers.

items.title: Cardholder data never stored outside PCI scope
items.body: PAN and CVV must not be logged, cached or persisted by any component outside the CDE trust boundary.

items.title: SSO for internal admin tools
items.body: Admin console access via Okta OIDC with SCIM de-provisioning within 1 hour.

items.title: Stripe is the payment processor
items.body: Contractual through 2028. Any design must work within Stripe Payment Intents.

items.title: US data residency
items.body: All customer PII stays in us-east-1 / us-west-2.

items.title: Holiday code freeze Nov 20 - Jan 2
items.body: Only P1 fixes, approved by the incident commander, may deploy during the freeze.

items.title: Peak traffic is 8x baseline on Black Friday
items.body: Based on 2024-2025 peaks (7.2x and 7.8x). Load tests target 8x with 25% headroom.

items.title: Stripe API meets its 99.99% SLA
items.body: Our 99.95% goal (#GOAL-2) assumes Stripe is not the dominant source of errors.

items.title: Thin Kafka operational expertise
items.body:
**Likelihood:** medium | **Impact:** high

Only one engineer has run Kafka in production. Mitigation: managed MSK (#ADR-1), runbooks, game day (#TICKET-27).

items.title: Inventory oversell during flash sales
items.body:
**Likelihood:** high | **Impact:** medium

Mitigated by reservations (#REQ-4).

items.title: Search reindex exceeds maintenance window
items.body: A full reindex takes ~5h today. Mitigation: blue/green aliases (#TICKET-26).

items.title: Stripe Payment Intents v2 migration window
items.body: Stripe deprecates v1 confirmation flow on **2027-03-01**. Sandbox access granted 2026-09-30.

items.title: Okta SCIM provisioning from Corporate IT
items.body: IT must enable the SCIM app integration (ticket IT-4471).

items.title: Checkout Modernization
items.body: Guest checkout, idempotency, Payment Intents v2 and the new address/shipping steps. GA target: **Nov 16**.

items.title: Event-Driven Order Pipeline
items.body: Replace synchronous fulfillment calls with `OrderPlaced` events on MSK via a transactional outbox.

items.title: Search & Catalog Performance
items.body: OpenSearch migration, caching and relevance work.

items.title: PCI Readiness
items.body: Everything needed to pass the PCI DSS 4.0 assessment (#GOAL-3).

items.title: Observability Foundation
items.body: OpenTelemetry tracing, SLOs and burn-rate alerting.

items.title: Use Amazon MSK (Kafka) for order events
items.body: We need durable, replayable, ordered-per-order events for fulfillment and future analytics consumers. Team Kafka experience is limited (#RISK-1). Spike: #SPIKE-1.
items.decisionOptions:
1. **SNS + SQS** - simple, fully managed; no replay, no ordering beyond FIFO groups.
2. **EventBridge** - schema registry, easy routing; 24h retry window, limited replay.
3. **Self-managed Kafka** - full control; high ops burden.
4. **Amazon MSK** - Kafka semantics, AWS-managed brokers.
items.decisionOutcome: Chosen: **Amazon MSK**. Replay and per-key ordering are must-haves; MSK removes most of the broker operations risk.
items.decisionConsequences:
- Good: consumers can replay 7 days of events.
- Good: per-order ordering via partition key.
- Bad: higher baseline cost than SNS/SQS (~$1.9k/mo).
- Neutral: need schema registry discipline.

items.title: Transactional outbox for event publishing
items.body: Dual writes (DB then Kafka) lose or duplicate events on partial failure, violating #REQ-7.
items.decisionOptions:
1. Dual write with retries
2. Debezium CDC on the orders table
3. Outbox table + polling relay
items.decisionOutcome: Outbox table written in the same transaction as the order; a relay publishes and marks rows sent.
items.decisionConsequences:
- Good: atomic with the order write.
- Bad: ~250ms publish latency from polling.
- Revisit CDC if latency matters.

items.title: Self-managed Elasticsearch on EC2 for search
items.body: Original 2024 decision for product search.
items.decisionConsequences: - Bad: patching and reindexing became a recurring burden (#RISK-3).

items.title: Use Amazon OpenSearch Service for product search
items.body: Replaces #ADR-3. Operating our own cluster costs ~1 engineer-week per month.
items.decisionOptions:
1. Stay on self-managed Elasticsearch
2. Amazon OpenSearch Service
3. Algolia (SaaS)
items.decisionOutcome: Amazon OpenSearch Service with blue/green index aliases.
items.decisionConsequences:
- Good: managed upgrades and snapshots.
- Bad: some Elastic-only plugins unavailable.

items.title: Tokenize cards with Stripe Elements
items.body: Keep raw PAN out of our systems to shrink PCI scope (#REQ-9) within our Stripe contract (#CON-1).
items.decisionOptions:
1. Server-side card collection
2. Stripe Elements (hosted fields)
3. Stripe Checkout redirect
items.decisionOutcome: Stripe Elements: card data goes browser -> Stripe directly; we only see tokens.
items.decisionConsequences:
- Good: SAQ A-EP instead of SAQ D for the storefront.
- Neutral: UI styling limited to Elements API.

items.title: Adopt OpenTelemetry for tracing
items.body: Needed for #REQ-8. Vendor-neutral instrumentation keeps the X-Ray vs Datadog decision open.
items.decisionOptions:
1. AWS X-Ray SDK
2. Datadog APM agent
3. OpenTelemetry SDK + collector
items.decisionOutcome: _Proposed:_ OpenTelemetry SDK, exporting to X-Ray via the ADOT collector.
items.decisionConsequences: - Open question: sampling strategy at 8x peak.

items.title: GraphQL BFF for the storefront
items.body: Evaluated to reduce mobile round-trips.
items.decisionOptions:
1. GraphQL BFF
2. REST with sparse fieldsets
items.decisionOutcome: Rejected: team capacity; REST + sparse fieldsets is sufficient.
items.decisionConsequences: - Revisit in 2027 if mobile payload size becomes a problem.

items.title: Store idempotency keys in Redis
items.body: Original approach for #REQ-2.
items.decisionConsequences: - Deprecated: Redis failover lost keys during a game day; keys now live in Postgres next to the order (#ADR-2).

items.title: Evaluate Kafka vs EventBridge vs SNS/SQS
items.body: Timeboxed to 3 days. Outcome recorded in #ADR-1.
